title.narrative: 1.3 Strengthen the Pacific ACP regional institutional capacities, systems and resources to support national implementation of the Paris Agreement in the context of the FRDP

description.narrative: (1) Conduct stocktake and mapping of regional organizations capabilities and expertise, systems and resources including political and technical capacities, and formal and informal partnerships, (2) Develop a regional support strategy for the implementation of the FRDP, (3) Strengthen regional coordination mechanism and optimize CROP support to Members in national implementation of global and regional frameworks

comment.narrative: 1. Past regional assessments were focused on certain capacity aspects of one or more agencies versus a holistic assessment.2. No integrated regional support strategy for implementation of FRDPPRP 2017

PACRES through PIFS facilitated strengthening political and technical capacities and understanding of both the FRDP and Paris Agreement through supporting the Political Climate Champions PCC initiative. The PCC brought together the regional technical agencies under the OneCROP mechanism the technical expertise from the national level covering specific negotiation streams of the Paris Agreement and the political champions nominated from the member countries who were at Ministerial level. PACRES supported a technical training and awareness session in the margins of the Forum Leaders meeting in 2022 which helped elevate the initiative and resulted in the expansion of the priority thematic areas from an initial 5 to 8 inclusive of gender. The PCC initiative was critical as when technical negotiations reached a hurdle at the global UNFCCC processes the Pacific had a fallback option through the Political Climate Champions. The PIFS PACRES Project Coordinator supported the political champions during their initial engagement at COP 26 and at COP 27. The PIFS Director for Programmes and Initiatives was supported by PACRES to attend COP 28 in Dubai in 2023 in support of the champions.PACRES participated in incountry missions to Kiribati and Papua New Guinea Cook Islands and FSM to socialize and gauge national level understanding of and operationalization of the FRDP. There is also interest from both Kiribati and Solomon Islands for potential development of National level FRDP plans. It must be noted that due COVID19 incountry missions from 20202021 were not possible due border closures and scheduling. SPREP through PACRES currently developing a SPREP FRDP Implementation Action Plan to be finalized prior to contractual enddate of SPREP FRDP Coordinator. Further to this PACRES through the FRDP Coordinator provided HighLevel Technical Briefing papers as well as convening technical briefing meetings and onsite support for several Political Climate Champions attending COP26 COP27 and COP28.

SPCPIFSSPREP leading the development of ME strategy and later the ME Framework Monitor all climate change and DRR aspects in the region and centered on the 3 goals of FRDP. 1CROP team development banks NGOs etc are continuously engagedPSIDS PreCOP27 Preparatory MeetingThe PSIDS PreCOP27 Preparatory meeting was convened from 2629 September and brought together participants from 13 Pacific countries both facetoface and virtually. The meeting served as the final preparatory platform for PSIDS to finalize its positions on specific thematic priorities find common ground on contentious issues and for enhancing coordination amongst PSIDS members and associated negotiating partners such as the Alliance of Small Island States AOSIS. The PACRES Project personnel were again involved in the development of thematic briefing notes presentations and logistical arrangements.Support to Young Negotiators at COP27 A for Call for Expression of Interests from students for COP27 was advertised through the USP all staff and students mailing list on 25Aug22. A total of 36 applications were received at the close of the call on 16Sep22. A selection panel consisting of two senior staff from USP and the PACRES USP PMT members reviewed all applications. A total of 5 students and staff 2 men and 3 women from USP were selected to attend COP27 in Sharm elSheikh in Egypt representing Fiji Solomon Islands Tonga and Tuvalu. A total of 9 students 3 men and 6 women were selected to provide backstopping support to the core team that will be travelling to Egypt.

title.narrative: 1.1 Support the Pacific Resilience partnership governance mechanisms to strengthen regional coordination on climate change and disaster resilience for effective implementation of the FRDP

description.narrative: (1) PRP Support Unit positions filled and operationalization of FRDP focal points (2) Pacific Resilience Partnership (PRP) Taskforce operationalised including working groups and/or committees (3) Pacific Resilience Meeting (biennial) (4) Technical Working Groups (TWGs) operationalised (TWGs Human Mobility, Localisation, Disaster Risk Finance, Information and Knowledge Management and Risk Governance

comment.narrative: No dedicated unit and staff to progress FRDPPRP 2017

Pacific Resilience partnership governance mechanisms operationalPRP Support Unit positions filled in SPREP SPC and PIFSPRP Taskforce operationalized in 2018 with approval of Governance structure by Forum Leaders including the establishment of five 5 initial TWGsPacific Resilience Meeting convened in 2019 2021 and 1113 October 20239 TWGs are established and operational.

SPREP recruited a FRDP coordinator 2 PRP TF face to face meeting 2 virtual meetings in 2019 and 3 PRP TF meeting in 2020 and 1 virtual meeting and regular updates with online decision making facilitated in 2021 PRM meeting held in 2019 and in July 2021 preceded by a youth prePRM meeting. PRP webinar Climate Resilience Pacific Youth Pathway to COP 26 held on 28 September. All FRDP focal points in place for SPREP SPC and PIFS and 5 TWG established and operationalPacific Resilience Partnership Taskforce had its first facetoface meeting on 18 19 July after over two years of virtual meetings. The meeting provided an opportunity to meet with new Taskforce members as well as update the Taskforce on developments since 2019. The PRP Taskforce provides strategic guidance over the PRP governance arrangements and the meeting provided that opportunity to bring everyone together. It was also an opportunity for the PRP Taskforce to discuss how they can continue to strengthen the multistakeholder and coordination aspect of the PRP as well as their representative role on the Taskforce.Three new PRP Technical Working Groups TWG have been established and include the Pacific based carbon mechanism Resilient Infrastructure and Resilient Housing Gender and Social Inclusion bringing the total number of TWG to eight 8. Two TWG are currently in the pipeline and include Disaster Waste and Water Security. These TWG will continue to provide a mechanism for enhancing coordination of related initiatives serve as a regional expert platform for networking and support to governments on these issues and promote and strengthen efforts to address these identified priority issues. As part of strengthening political and technical capacities and understanding of the Paris Agreement a working dialogue of was held on 10 July 2022 that brought together the Political Climate Champions an initiative aimed at strengthening the linkages between the political and technical negotiations for stronger beneficial outcomes to the Pacific and the technical advisors leading on identified thematic areas under the Paris Agreement. The dialogue was held in the margins of the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting as a means to continue to elevate recognition of the role of the Political Climate Champions in the UNFCCC meetings. In the Communique of the 51st Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting Leaders supported the work of the Political Climate Champions to strengthen the Forum Island Countries strategic engagement at COP27 including the nomination of a new Champion on Gender and Social Inclusion.

title.narrative: 1.2 Scale up the institutional capacity and knowledge of the Pacific ACP regional organizations to serve the needs of national governments in climate change negotiations during UNFCCC sessions and processes, aiming for increased use of climate science and best practices to inform negotiations and for a more balanced representation of women and young people

description.narrative: (1) Organize annual preCOP preparatory platform, (2) Support for Pacific ACP countries during UNFCCC meetings and prepare & disseminate postCOP analysis to synthesize negotiations in priority areas, (3) Establish southsouth negotiations mentoring with other ACP regions, (4) Increased climate science inputs to inform negotiations, (5) New and young negotiators participate in and contribute to briefing and negotiation training for 1CROP team to support Pacific ACP on UNFCCC negotiations

comment.narrative: PreCOP 26 58 September 2021. 45 participants 26 women 19 men trained on COP processes in a virtual PreCOP training 27 participants 25 16 females 9 males trained on COP processes 2 1 female 1 male supported for the SPREPled negotiator training. 6 3 females 3 males participated in COP 25 in Madrid Spain. 7 6 women 1 man participants participated in the virtual SPREPled negotiator training for COP26. 14 10 women 4 men participants participated virtually in COP26 Post COP 26 analysis held in February 2022 Caribbean being part of the PSIDS COP analysis programmeThere have been several significant events convened in this quarter in relation to the UNFCCC climate change negotiations at both technical and political levels2nd Pacific Political Climate Champions MeetingThe Political Climate Champions mechanism and inaugural meeting was established and convened in 2021 prior to COP26. description.narrative: (1) PRP Support Unit positions filled and operationalization of FRDP focal points (2) Pacific Resilience Partnership (PRP) Taskforce operationalised including working groups and/or committees (3) Pacific Resilience Meeting (biennial) (4) Technical Working Groups (TWGs) operationalised (TWGs Human Mobility, Localisation, Disaster Risk Finance, Information and Knowledge Management and Risk Governance

comment.narrative: SPREP recruited a FRDP coordinator 2 PRP TF face to face meeting 2 virtual meetings in 2019 and 3 PRP TF meeting in 2020 and 1 virtual meeting and regular updates with online decision making facilitated in 2021 PRM meeting held in 2019 and in July 2021 preceded by a youth prePRM meeting. PRP webinar Climate Resilience Pacific Youth Pathway to COP 26 held on 28 September. All FRDP focal points in place for SPREP SPC and PIFS and 5 TWG established and operationalPacific Resilience Partnership Taskforce had its first facetoface meeting on 18 19 July after over two years of virtual meetings. The meeting provided an opportunity to meet with new Taskforce members as well as update the Taskforce on developments since 2019. The PRP Taskforce provides strategic guidance over the PRP governance arrangements and the meeting provided that opportunity to bring everyone together. It was also an opportunity for the PRP Taskforce to discuss how they can continue to strengthen the multistakeholder and coordination aspect of the PRP as well as their representative role on the Taskforce.Three new PRP Technical Working Groups TWG have been established and include the Pacific based carbon mechanism Resilient Infrastructure and Resilient Housing Gender and Social Inclusion bringing the total number of TWG to eight 8. Two TWG are currently in the pipeline and include Disaster Waste and Water Security. These TWG will continue to provide a mechanism for enhancing coordination of related initiatives serve as a regional expert platform for networking and support to governments on these issues and promote and strengthen efforts to address these identified priority issues. As part of strengthening political and technical capacities and understanding of the Paris Agreement a working dialogue of was held on 10 July 2022 that brought together the Political Climate Champions an initiative aimed at strengthening the linkages between the political and technical negotiations for stronger beneficial outcomes to the Pacific and the technical advisors leading on identified thematic areas under the Paris Agreement. The dialogue was held in the margins of the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting as a means to continue to elevate recognition of the role of the Political Climate Champions in the UNFCCC meetings. In the Communique of the 51st Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting Leaders supported the work of the Political Climate Champions to strengthen the Forum Island Countries strategic engagement at COP27 including the nomination of a new Champion on Gender and Social Inclusion.

The FRDP ME Framework has been developed and validated and being aligned with the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific MEL Framework.The FRDP ME Framework with technical guidelines was developed based on 4 pilot countries including Fiji Tonga Kiribati and Vanuatu and was presented to Pacific Island Forum Leaders in 2019 for their noting. Noting the ongoing restrictions on travel the initial draft FRDP ME Framework was validated through desk top research assessing the remaining 12 PICTs national development plans climate change and disaster risk management policies. The FRDP ME indicators were updated to reflect common indicators across the 16 Pacific Island Forum Countries and Territories that aligned with the 3 goals of the FRDP and aligned with relevant indicators under the SDG Sendai Framework and the Paris Agreement. Adaptation pilot includes i.Papua New Guinea building resilience to climate change and natural disasters in Karama and nearby communities Malalaua District Papua New Guinea mangrove nursery maintenance and planting rapid agriculture assessment to support new food cultivars developed a flood food and water security focussed disaster management plan established 3 rainwater catchments. Establishment of 10 rainwater harvesting systems in the Alukuni Karawa and Keapara primary school including solar lights in Keapara village Rigo District Central Province inclusive of water safety campaigns. Strengthening climate change and disaster resilience networks and identify financing opportunities with stakeholders in PNG via a workshop.ii.Samoa enhanced water security in the Matautu district by installing 100 rainwaters harvesting systems in total in the villages of Saleia Safai Satoalepai Fagamalo Lelepa Avao and Vaipouli villages strengthening institution arrangements and coordination mechanisms for adaptation and mitigation planning and implementation through national workshops in preparation for negotiations and representative at COP 27 and 28 Samoa being the chair for PSIDSAOSIS finalised the forestry regulations and forestry policy EbA options assessment for Saleaula bay Lagoon water quality is a complex issue with freshwater seeping into lagoon from underwater springs and the development of the Masamasafalelima National Park management Plan.iii.Solomon Islands Expansion of the Barana Nature Heritage Park BNHP boundaries to include the whole Mataniko catchment and parts of LungaBetikamaBoko catchment Honiara water source UXO Bomb Survey of the site and explore and implement local ecofriendly technology materials and alternatives used bamboos for riverbank stabilisation and riparian zone rehabilitation expanded the BNHP forestry nursery reforestation of the BNHP and development of the Botanic Gardens Landscape Architecture master Plan including survey and Honiara CBD Greening and Landscaping Master Plan.iv.TimorLeste conducted integrated vulnerability assessments in 6 villages with an intention to identify most vulnerable and implement project activities in. Establishment of water systems from a nearby spring to provide water to 110 households in Haupu Ermera District and borehole water system to 166 households in Larisula Baucau District and training of the Climate Change Office staffs on risk and vulnerability mapping and GIS.v.Vanuatu riverbank stabilisation and riparian zone rehabilitation using vetiver grasses and indigenous tree fruit species Tagabe forestry nursery expansion nursery staffs training for seed collection storage and planting in nurser community groups engaged to plant tree seedlings and wildings in the Tagabe watershed developed the Port Vila greening master plan and the Tagabe Integrated Catchment Management Plan reviewed the department of climate change organisation structure and inter sectoral arrangements to support EbA solutions and training of relevant government officials and nonstate actors in joint planning to strengthen coordination for implementing EbA solutions

description.narrative: (1) Support the Pacific Regional Federation of Resilience Professionals (PRFRP), (2) Revise the TVET resilience qualifications Levels 1 4 to include monitoring & reporting tools and mechanisms and integrated guidelines on resilience, (3) Scale up technical and vocational education and training (TVET) capacity building by developing qualification in resilience Level 5 6, (4) Provide support through regular dialogue and knowledge exchange with the PRFRP, (5) Exchange experience and good practice within the Pacific and, where applicable, with other ACP regions for Pacific ACP resilience, (6) Establish & formalize resilience sector as a community of practice, (7) Support for existing climate change and climate related Pacific ACP networks, (8) SouthSouth Cooperation in relation to Government and Private Sector

comment.narrative: The review and revision of Resilience Qualification Levels 1 2 has been completed and renamed the Articulated Resilience Qualification Level 2. Articulated Level 2 collapses Levels 12 and has addressed the content overlap of the existing qualification. The new qualification enables training institutions to address country specific requirements. The revised qualification level has been submitted to Educational Quality Assessment Programme EQAP for regional accreditation. Level 3 4 is completed Development of Resilience Qualification Levels 56 is underway using hybrid meetings in person and online to accommodate participation of the regional experts. The first draft was updated during the first hybrid meeting and the updated document shared with the experts for their validation.As part of the rollout of Resilience qualifications the provision of TVET tools has commenced with the Ministry of Youth on 21st July 2022. The tools and equipment were composed of 6 Laptop Computers and 5 Garmin Etres Handheld GPS. In order for the trainers to be conversant and skilled in the use of such tools and equipment the PACRES project provided training on the Use of Handheld GPS in July 2022. The training was in partnership with the SPC GEMOceans and Maritime program. There were 15 participants during the whole day training at the MOY campus in Nasau in Sigatoka.An indepth orientation on the Resilience Qualification delivery has been conducted in July which were participated in by the representatives of the TVET sector practitioners in resilience and partners in SPC engaged in CCDRR worksTo date the CoP billboards has been staked in the 3 villages in Nadroga and 1 in Tavua. The CoP has been expanded and now includes Vanuakula in Tavua and 2 IndoFIjian villages in Nadroga Vunakavika and Tulalevu. The signing of pledges and staking of billboards in the additional villages are set for the end of October 2022. As the CoP engagement continues the interventions provided to the communities are centred on Building a resilient community through selfreliance. A series of Learning Sessions are in the pipeline up to the end of 2022. The learning sessions are catered separately for the village decisionmakers and members of the community. In some instances the interventions are participated in by the entire community populace. It must be noted that the activities in the IndoFijian communities are done in the evenings since the people are working in the cane field in the daytime. Additionally a sevusevu in the IndoFijian communities are also done as part of the traditional protocol where an ITaukei village landowner must be acknowledged.

description.narrative: (1) Map out and take stock of private sector resilience building initiatives, (2i) Develop a regional capacity building programme for private sector, (2ii) Preparation of legislative & policy reforms to strengthen private sector engagement, investment in resilient development & access to climate finance, (2iii) Setting up partnerships with more experienced enterprises through Private Sector SouthSouth Cooperation arrangements, 3) Conduct meetings and workshops with private sector stakeholders

comment.narrative: 1. No private sector stakeholders consulted or engaged 2. No dedicated capacity building programme for the private sector3. No reforms supported by the project

Total number of private sector representatives engaged 693. These were representatives who attended the private sector mapping related workshop businesses who were consulted during the mapping exercise those who participated during the Melanesia Micronesia and Polynesia Subregional private sector climate finance dialogues national consultations peertopeer learning and the regional online training with USP TAFE. The subregional workshop on climate finance for the private sector is a platform for information sharing and learning for the private sector and an opportunity to network with government representatives through the NDA Office. A total of 6 subregional workshops would have been completed. PIFS collaborated with USP TAFE to develop targeted courses for the private sector that commenced in January to June 2023. Two courses were developed related to Climate Resilience for Business Sustainability III to address the challenge of lack of technical knowledge and skills by the private sector. There were more than 300 expressions of interest received but the applications had to be vetted with only 105 candidates selected. The first Pacific regional peertopeer leaning programme for the private sector was another activity where nine 9 NPSO representatives from the region visited Fiji businesses to learn and share about climate and resilience actions including disaster preparedness. Fiji Commerce Employers Federation Fiji Business Disaster Resilience Council with support from PIFS PACRES cohosted the regional private sector participants. Ten 10 businesses and two 2 government agencies were the organisations visited. Other international organisations saw value in the programme and decided to be part of it i.e. UN Connecting Business initiative CBi and UN Office of Humanitarian Coordination Affairs OCHA There will be at least 6 engagement strategies for Fiji KiribatiSamoa Tuvalu Palau and FSM developed to promote collaboration and strengthen partnership between the public and private sectors. These were developed as part of the mapping deliverables and these drafts were consulted widely amongst the stakeholders. PIFS PACRES worked with CBi Vanuatu Business Resilience Council Fiji Business Disaster Resilience Council setup the Solomon Islands Business Resilience Council within the Chamber of Commerce.

26 Cook Islands national private sector mapping participants. 52 combined private sector for Cook Is and subregional participants 88 private sector and stakeholders engaged for Solomon Is and Tonga private sector mapping Fiji Private Sector Mapping completed about 38 business representatives were consulted. Finalisation of tender for the Kiribati private sector mapping to begin in Qtr 1 2022 and preparation for the Tuvalu private sector mapping drafting of ToR and discussing with TNPSO 1 Polynesia subregional workshop 5 two subregional workshops and 3 countries for P2P learning programs. Virtual Melanesia Subregional workshop held on 2122 September 2021. 97 registered with 3040 attended on each day of the Melanesia Subregional private sector workshop. 2087 attended the Micronesia subregional workshop. Finalised technical support details with Samoa Chamber of Commerce and Fiji Commerce Employers Federation with terms of reference for the consultants drafted. Private sector mapping was completed for Kiribati on 29 July 2022 with the final deliverables of the consultant being reviewed jointly by the Kiribati Chamber of Commerce and Industry Climate Change Office and the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat PIFS. Tuvalu private sector mapping was initiated on 09 September 2022 with a shortterm consultant being engaged to work with the Tuvalu National Private Sector Organisation and the Department of Climate Change. Private sector mapping reports for Samoa Vanuatu Fiji and Tonga are currently being finalised and to be published once cleared by the relevant national private sector organisations. A tender has been advertised for a shortterm consultant to work under the guidance of the Vanuatu Business Resilience Council to build capacity of the private sector in climate change and resilience and explore opportunities to support private sector initiatives and climate actions. A Letter of Agreement was signed between the Solomon Islands Chamber of Commerce and Industry and PIFS that is effective for one year from 06 September 2022 to recognise and formalise the cooperation and support in the PACRES Project Workplan. The Polynesia SubRegional Private Sector Climate Finance Workshop was successfully convened in a hybrid mode where representatives from the private sector and the Green Climate Fund National Designated Authority from Cook Islands Niue Samoa Tonga and Tuvalu converged in Apia from the 2729 September. There were more than sixty participants who attended inperson at the Lava Hotel conference room including some who joined virtually. The threeday workshop ended with a tree planting programme organised by Samoas Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment at the Vailima and Botanical Garden and Reserve.
